belief: I'm a disappointment to my parents.
origins: When grades or milestones are lower than a parent hoped, children can sense disappointment, spoken or not. As adults, they may still hear it, and some parents did say hurtful things.
teaches: “Though my father and mother forsake me, the LORD will receive me.” “Before I formed you in the womb I knew you.” “Can a woman forget her nursing child…? Even if she could forget, I will not forget you!” God’s view of you is not shaped by anyone’s expectations. Honor your parents, grieve what hurt, and let your Heavenly Father define you. Many parents also change and learn to see their child’s strengths.
self_statements: I will never make them proud.
I am a failure to them.
errors: Believing I am either a pride or a disappointment.
Predicting they will never accept me.
Feeling their disappointment and concluding I am one.
questions: What did my parents actually say, and what did I assume?
What do I wish they could see?
What are my parents’ own fears or hopes?
What does God say about me?
Is it possible to talk with them?
How can I honor them while defining myself differently?
truth: My worth is not set by my parents’ approval. God received me, knew me, and loves me. I can honor my parents, speak honestly if possible, and let God define me.
hw_truths: He knew me before I was born.
I am fearfully and wonderfully made.
log: Each week, note one thing God says about you.
prayer: Father, I have felt like a disappointment. Thank You that You receive me. Heal the hurt, and help me honor my parents while resting in Your love. Amen.
